synthesis.overall_assessment: The assigned range is a broad concept-control inventory with a consistently enforced non-production boundary. Most controls are intentionally unpromoted and therefore cannot be treated as buildable. The strongest exact contract is the distinct Revert/Rewind wiring pair; the largest adversarial risks are ungoverned YOLO authority, undefined interrupt/cancel and recovery state, misleading operational status, inaccessible custom click targets, unbounded fan-out/concurrency, untrusted composer/file inputs, and unsafe worktree transitions.
cross_window_findings: Concept-only owner adjudication is consistent and blocks accidental promotion, but generic owner references do not close callers, consumers, or cross-document seams.
Production-looking status and controls frequently have null command and wiring identities, so visible state cannot be accepted as runtime truth.
Custom div/span interactions repeatedly lack role, keyboard parity, selected/disabled state, and recovery behavior.
Operationally sensitive actions require explicit authority, state, receipt, idempotency, partial-failure, and rollback contracts before promotion.
Fixture exclusions and the Revert/Rewind command distinction are explicit and should be preserved as non-gaps.
residual_unknowns: Which canonical owner documents and production consumers will adjudicate each concept-only control.
How shared selection, active-run, worktree, context, and authority state is versioned and synchronized across concurrent actions.
Which data retention, privacy, localization, offline, scale, and support policies apply when these controls are promoted.
What receipt schemas and executable acceptance oracles prove state provenance, destructive recovery, and cross-document compatibility.
